headline: German robot maker Neura Robotics has launched an AI model that lets robots combine sight, touch and sound and remember objects they can no longer see.
score_reason: Fresh product launch of interest to robotics, but all claims are the company's and a public demo is still a week away.
importance_line: Factories that want robots to do fiddly tasks such as fitting parts could benefit, but the performance claims come from Neura and have not been independently tested.
source: Robotics & Automation News, citing Neura Robotics
summary: Robotics & Automation News reports, in an item based on Neura Robotics' announcement, that the German company launched Neuron AI, a model that combines 3D vision, touch, force, audio and language with a memory so a robot can keep track of objects out of sight. Neura plans to show its 4NE1 humanoid doing an eleven-minute laundry sequence with the model at Nvidia's GTC Berlin event on 20 to 22 Oct; until then the capabilities are the company's own claims.
notes: Company press release relayed by the outlet; demo is future.
